record.jurisdiction: Greater San Francisco Bay Area (nine counties plus Monterey, San Benito, Santa Cruz and San Joaquin) and Sacramento County
record.program_name: Housing Trust Silicon Valley short term loans (predevelopment, acquisition, construction/rehab and bridge)
record.administering_agency: Housing Trust Silicon Valley (CDFI; California Finance Lender License 6053356), 75 E. Santa Clara Street Suite 1350, San Jose; lending team Nick Friend (408-703-3837 ext. 223, nick@housingtrustsv.org) and Stephaney Kipple (ext. 244)
record.typical_award_size: Loans sized to project need; recent closings: $1,500,000 predevelopment for Gateway Tower, San Jose (220 units, 30% to 70% AMI, The Core Companies, 2026); $2,000,000 predevelopment for 69th Street Apartments, Sacramento (129 units, 30% to 60% AMI, CRP Affordable Housing, third Sacramento loan since expansion); acquisition loans up to about $9.9 million in Santa Cruz County (2025). Housing Trust reports $785 million invested since 2000. Capitalized by the TECH Fund (Cisco, Packard Foundation, Google, Grove Foundation, Sobrato Family Foundation, LinkedIn, NetApp, Pure Storage, Jewish Community Federation) and the Affordable Housing Growth Fund and 2015 Loan Pool (Avidbank, Beneficial State Bank, Bridge Bank, East West Bank, First Bank, Fremont Bank, Heritage Bank of Commerce, Manufacturers Bank, Presidio Bank, Silicon Valley Bank, Tech CU).
record.affordability_requirement: Affordable rental and ownership housing for low income households; mixed income allowed with affordability restrictions; underwriting per Housing Trust term sheets (acquisition, bridge and predevelopment term sheets are provided by the lending team, not posted).
record.next_deadline: Rolling; every loan starts with a call to the lending team.
record.layering_notes: The largest regional nonprofit lender in the footprint. Footprint confirmed from Just Funded posts: Santa Clara, San Mateo, Alameda, Contra Costa, Santa Cruz, Monterey, Sonoma and, since about 2024, Sacramento County (three loans). Use for predevelopment and acquisition before TCAC/CDLAC awards; loans repay at construction or permanent closing. Housing Trust is also a Golden State Acquisition Fund originator and partners with FHLBank San Francisco on Affordable Housing Program grants (for example $2 million for 2700 International, Oakland). Separate records cover the Apple Affordable Housing Fund, Supportive Housing Fund (Santa Clara County), Monterey Bay Housing Trust and Sonoma County Housing Fund. Private capital, so no prevailing wage trigger from this source alone.
record.audit_note: Nov 8, 2026 spot check: the program page posts no loan terms; term sheets come from the lending team. The page describes geography as the greater Bay Area. Recent loans were confirmed in Just Funded posts: Gateway Tower $1,500,000 predevelopment and 2727 Mattison Lane $9,945,000 acquisition (April 2025). The 69th Street post (Oct 30, 2024) confirms the Sacramento loan, but the excerpt read did not show the amount. prevailing_wage_trigger false is not backed by a cited rule; it rests on the source being private capital.

record.jurisdiction: Greater San Francisco Bay Area (13 counties)
record.program_name: Apple Affordable Housing Fund (Housing Trust Silicon Valley), annual Request for Information
record.administering_agency: Housing Trust Silicon Valley (CDFI; California Finance Lender License 6053356), 75 E. Santa Clara Street Suite 1350, San Jose; lending team Nick Friend (408-703-3837 ext. 223, nick@housingtrustsv.org) and Stephaney Kipple (ext. 244); inquiries applefund@housingtrustsv.org
record.typical_award_size: RFI Round 7 (September 1 to October 1, 2026): most loans $2 million to $5 million, higher considered; construction/bridge up to 36 months interest only; construction to mini-perm 5, 7 or 10 year terms (20 or 30 year amortization); construction to permanent up to 20 years; interest up to 3% during construction and 2% permanent; combined loan to cost up to 95% with subordinate debt; origination fee greater of 1% or $30,000, $15,000 application fee credited at closing, $10,000 conversion fee, 0.15% annual monitoring fee. Fund is up to $150 million from Apple's 2019 $2.5 billion California housing commitment; 4 to 5 projects selected per round.
record.affordability_requirement: Deed-restricted affordable housing, incomes from extremely low up to 120% AMI; must add net new affordable units; if using LIHTC, must apply to CDLAC or TCAC in 2026 or 2027.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. Round 7 RFI closed October 1, 2026; Housing Trust has not announced Round 8.
record.layering_notes: Eligible counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Monterey, Napa, San Benito, San Francisco, San Joaquin, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Solano and Sonoma. Readiness is the key screen: construction must start by December 31, 2027 and awards are not held past that date. Two proposals per developer. Designed to fill gaps for shovel-ready deals waiting on state awards; repayment from permanent financing including AHSC or Infill Infrastructure Grant proceeds is expected. Full recourse and completion guaranty during construction; first or second deed of trust, subordinate only to a bank construction or permanent lender.
record.cycle_notes: Annual Request for Information. Round 7 (2026): RFI released September 1, 2026, information session September 15, 2026, questions due September 16, 2026, final FAQs September 23, 2026, submissions due October 1, 2026 at 5pm PDT; move to underwriting estimated December 2026, credit committee notifications rolling. Page shows Round 7 as closed and gives no Round 8 date; prior rounds opened each September, so a fall 2027 round is likely but not announced. Projects must be shovel ready by December 31, 2027.
record.audit_note: Tier 2 deadline audit 2026-11-08: Round 7 closed October 1, 2026; next round not announced on the agency page. Removed the unsourced 'Round 8 expected about September 2027' from next_deadline and noted it as an inference in cycle_notes.

record.jurisdiction: Monterey Bay region (Santa Cruz, Monterey and San Benito Counties)

record.administering_agency: Housing Trust Silicon Valley (CDFI; California Finance Lender License 6053356), 75 E. Santa Clara Street Suite 1350, San Jose; lending team Nick Friend (408-703-3837 ext. 223, nick@housingtrustsv.org) and Stephaney Kipple (ext. 244) with the Monterey Bay Economic Partnership; Dignity Health is a financing partner
record.typical_award_size: Revolving fund created July 2016 that exceeded its $10 million initial raise by summer 2017; loans for acquisition, predevelopment or construction sized to project need (Housing Trust reports 14 loans totaling about $33 million in the Monterey Bay region, including a $9,945,000 acquisition loan for 2727 Mattison Lane in Santa Cruz County in 2025).
record.affordability_requirement: Affordable housing for low income individuals and families and those with special needs.
record.next_deadline: Rolling; contact the Housing Trust lending team.
record.layering_notes: Covers Santa Cruz, San Benito and Monterey Counties. The Santa Cruz County record from Pass 2 lists specific Santa Cruz loans; this regional record covers the fund itself. Loans typically repay at construction or permanent closing, so sequence ahead of TCAC, County Housing Funds and Salinas or Watsonville local funds.
record.audit_note: Nov 8, 2026 spot check: the page confirms the July 2016 launch, the fund exceeding its $10 million goal, acquisition, predevelopment and construction uses, the three-county footprint and Dignity Health as partner. The $9,945,000 Mattison Lane acquisition loan was confirmed in a Housing Trust post; the 14 loans and about $33 million regional total were not found on the pages read. prevailing_wage_trigger false is not backed by a cited rule; it rests on the source being private capital.

record.jurisdiction: Northern California and Bay Area region (statewide lender)
record.program_name: Century Housing Corporation acquisition and bridge loans
record.administering_agency: Century Housing Corporation (nonprofit CDFI), 1000 Corporate Pointe, Culver City; statewide lending to California borrowers
record.typical_award_size: $1,000,000 to $50,000,000; loan to value up to 100%, typically 90% of the lesser of appraised value or price; origination 1.0% to 2.0%; variable or fixed rate; term up to 5 years including extensions, no prepayment penalty; interest reserve capitalized; application fee up to $10,000 (refundable), legal up to $20,000; 30 to 45 day closings.
record.affordability_requirement: Developments affordable to households at or below 120% AMI; mixed-use eligible.
record.layering_notes: Regional activity confirmed on Century's site: Foon Lok East, Oakland (MidPen, $12,262,000 permanent loan, 125 units); Civic Center Drive, Santa Clara (Charities Housing, with Housing Trust Silicon Valley); Vista Verde Apartments, Santa Cruz County (Eden Housing, 72 units); Ross Gardens, Fresno (140 units, permanent loan). Century is a Golden State Acquisition Fund originator, so GSAF leverage can raise LTV. Borrowers include nonprofits, for-profits, cities and counties. Loans are recourse with a first deed of trust. Century's Emerging Developers Program (special purpose credit program, $15 million JPMorgan Chase facility and $10 million U.S. Bank racial equity bond) is available to minority- and women-owned developers statewide; the examples posted are in Los Angeles.

record.jurisdiction: Northern California and Bay Area region (statewide lender)
record.program_name: Century Housing Corporation construction loans
record.administering_agency: Century Housing Corporation (nonprofit CDFI), Culver City; statewide
record.typical_award_size: $1,000,000 to $27,000,000; up to 75% loan to value and 75% loan to cost; 12 to 24 month term with extensions; variable pricing plus origination, administrative, legal and third-party report fees; interest reserve funded from loan proceeds; progress-based draws.
record.affordability_requirement: Multifamily development with rents at or below 120% AMI.
record.layering_notes: Repaid through permanent financing (Century permanent loans, CCRC or bank take-outs). First deed of trust and assignment of rents, full recourse to sponsors. Works alongside LIHTC equity and state soft debt; confirm Century's position relative to any tax-exempt bond construction loan.

record.jurisdiction: Northern California and Bay Area region (statewide lender)
record.program_name: Century Housing Corporation permanent loans
record.administering_agency: Century Housing Corporation (nonprofit CDFI), Culver City; statewide
record.typical_award_size: $1,000,000 minimum; loan to value up to 90% (80% non-LIHTC); debt coverage 1.15 minimum (1.20 non-LIHTC); amortization up to 35 years; term up to 18 years including extensions; forward commitment up to 36 months; fixed rate; origination 1.0% to 2.0%; application fee up to $10,000, legal up to $20,000; 30 to 45 day closings.
record.affordability_requirement: Developments affordable to households at or below 120% AMI; mixed-use eligible.
record.layering_notes: Non-recourse first deed of trust. The 18-year maximum term is designed to run through the 15-year LIHTC compliance period. Compare with CCRC permanent loans (up to 35-year term) and bank or Freddie Mac TEL executions when sizing hard debt under TCAC underwriting.

record.jurisdiction: Northern California and Bay Area region (statewide lender)
record.program_name: California Community Reinvestment Corporation (CCRC) permanent loans for affordable multifamily housing
record.administering_agency: California Community Reinvestment Corporation (bank consortium CDFI), 225 W. Broadway Suite 120, Glendale; contact Jennifer Quevedo, jennifer.quevedo@e-ccrc.org, 818-550-9804
record.typical_award_size: Term up to 35 years (terms over 20 years reset the rate at year 16); amortization up to 35 years; rate lock up to 42 months; loan to value up to 85% for LIHTC properties and 80% non-LIHTC; minimum DSCR 1.15 LIHTC and 1.20 non-LIHTC; $10,000 application fee plus origination of the greater of 1% or $15,000; conversion at 95% occupancy for 90 days with 90% of tax credit equity funded; prepayment greater of yield maintenance or 1% until 90 days before maturity. Terms last updated September 2026. Recent regional loans: The Starling, Oakland (Eden Housing, 70 senior units, $6,721,000); Solaire Apartments, San Jose (January 2025, tax-exempt loan with 4% LIHTC); Creekside Trails, San Diego (October 2024 bridge loan).
record.affordability_requirement: Multifamily rental housing affordable to low income families, seniors and residents with special needs; mixed income properties at least 51% affordable at 80% AMI or below.
record.layering_notes: CCRC lends through a taxable mortgage pool funded by member banks and by directly purchasing tax-exempt bonds, which gives member banks CRA credit. It uses one set of pre-negotiated construction-to-permanent documents with Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, First Citizens Bank, JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America, so pairing a CCRC forward commitment with one of those construction lenders shortens closing. Appraisal is shared with the construction lender. Statewide footprint with Bay Area, Sacramento Valley and San Diego deals in its portfolio.
record.audit_note: Nov 8, 2026 spot check: the Permanent Financing term sheet (updated September 2026) matches on term, rate reset, amortization, rate lock, LTV, DSCR, fees and conversion. The 51% at 80% AMI mixed income rule appears on the bridge term sheet, not the permanent sheet.

record.jurisdiction: Northern California and Bay Area region (statewide lender)
record.program_name: California Community Reinvestment Corporation (CCRC) bridge and refinance loans for occupied affordable properties
record.administering_agency: California Community Reinvestment Corporation (bank consortium CDFI), Glendale; contact Jennifer Quevedo, 818-550-9804
record.typical_award_size: Bridge loans to repay a maturing first mortgage ahead of recapitalization: term up to 5 years with up to 2 years interest only case by case; amortization the lesser of 35 years or 10 years less than remaining economic life; minimum DSCR 1.20; full recourse at CCRC discretion; prepayment greater of yield maintenance or 1%, waived if refinanced by a CCRC loan. Proceeds may fund closing costs, immediate repairs from a property condition assessment and sustainability improvements including an energy audit. Refinance loan terms are posted separately (updated September 2026).
record.affordability_requirement: Occupied affordable multifamily properties with five or more units; mixed income properties at least 51% affordable at 80% AMI or lower.
record.layering_notes: A preservation tool for Year 15 and maturing-debt portfolios ahead of a 4% resyndication. Combine with state LHTF-funded local trust funds or county preservation NOFAs, and with the Bay Area Preservation Pilot where the property is in a transit area.
record.audit_note: Nov 8, 2026 spot check: the bridge term sheet matches. The separate Refinance Loan sheet (September 2026) offers loans up to $20,000,000, a term of up to 20 years, up to 80% LTV, 1.20x DSCR, and non-recourse terms with carve-outs. Rents must be at least 10% below market, with 20% of units at 50% AMI, 40% at 60% AMI or 51% at 80% AMI, and a regulatory agreement that outlasts the loan. Fees are a $15,000 application fee plus 1% to 1.5% origination.

record.jurisdiction: Northern California and Bay Area region (statewide lender)
record.program_name: Low Income Investment Fund (LIIF) affordable housing lending (acquisition, predevelopment, construction, bridge and term loans)
record.administering_agency: Low Income Investment Fund (national CDFI headquartered in San Francisco); Western Region lending contact Emma Chavez, Market Director, echavez@liifund.org, 213-262-2490 ext. 490; lending@liifund.org
record.typical_award_size: Products: acquisition and predevelopment loans, construction loans, term loans, construction-to-permanent, bridge loans, NMTC leverage loans and CDFI Bond Guarantee Program loans; 65 loans closed in FY24 and $292 million closed in FY23 (77% affordable housing); LIIF's affordable housing lending totals $1.2 billion. Loan sizes and rates are not posted; recent California examples include $1.5 million in predevelopment loans in Murrieta (Riverside County) and the JFM Seniors and Family apartments in the Coachella Valley.
record.affordability_requirement: Affordable homeownership and multifamily rental for low income households; below-market pricing where philanthropic capital allows.
record.layering_notes: LIIF is fund manager for the Golden State Acquisition Fund ($292 million, eight CDFI originators), the Bay Area Transit Oriented Affordable Housing Fund ($40 million), the Bay Area Preservation Pilot (with Enterprise) and We Lift, the Coachella Valley Housing Catalyst Fund ($50 million), each recorded separately. Its affiliate National Affordable Housing Trust syndicates LIHTC. Statewide activity 'from Crescent City to San Diego' per LIIF; Bay Area and Southern California concentrations.
record.audit_note: Nov 8, 2026 spot check: the page confirms the product list (it also lists tenant improvement loans), 65 loans closed in FY24 and the lending@liifund.org contact. The $292 million FY23 and $1.2 billion housing totals are not on this page, and no loan sizes are posted.

record.jurisdiction: Northern California and Bay Area region (statewide lender)
record.program_name: Enterprise Community Loan Fund (ECLF) loan products for affordable housing
record.administering_agency: Enterprise Community Loan Fund (Enterprise Community Partners' CDFI, S&P AA-); Northern California office in San Francisco; senior loan officer Eve Goldstein-Siegel, egoldstein@enterprisecommunity.org, 415-400-0986
record.typical_award_size: Predevelopment up to $2 million, up to 24 months; acquisition up to $8 million, up to 24 months, LTV up to 60% for vacant land and 80% for cash-flowing property; construction up to $10 million, up to 24 months, LTV up to 80%; bridge up to $10 million, up to 48 months against LIHTC or historic credit equity and other committed sources; mini-permanent and NMTC leverage up to $8 million, 5 to 7 years, LTV up to 75%; permanent up to $10 million, 7 or more years. Fees up to 2% of loan amount plus legal; full recourse. ECLF has invested $3.27 billion nationally with $648 million under management.
record.affordability_requirement: Affordable rental and for-sale housing, mixed-use and community facilities serving low income communities.
record.layering_notes: Northern California activity confirmed on Enterprise's regional page: $7.1 million construction loan for CHISPA's Vista de la Terraza in Salinas (40 farmworker family homes). Enterprise co-manages the Bay Area Preservation Pilot with LIIF, originates for the Golden State Acquisition Fund and the Bay Area TOAH Fund, co-leads BAHFA pilot programs and runs the Central Valley Housing Initiatives across eight Central Valley counties. Kaiser Permanente's $50 million RxHome loan to ECLF and the Housing for Health Fund (Bay Area and Sacramento preservation equity) also run through Enterprise; see the Kaiser record.
record.audit_note: Nov 8, 2026 spot check: all product maximums, terms and LTVs match. Permanent loans are non-recourse with carve-outs, not full recourse. Mini-permanent loans amortize up to 25 years and permanent loans up to 30 years.

record.jurisdiction: Five Bay Area counties (San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Alameda, Contra Costa)
record.program_name: Partnership for the Bay's Future: Bay's Future Fund (BFF) loans
record.administering_agency: LISC Bay Area (fund manager and originator) with Corporation for Supportive Housing and Capital Impact Partners as originators; San Francisco Foundation convener; contact Asha Rao, Senior Director of Investments, LISC Bay Area
record.typical_award_size: $500 million loan fund; structures from predevelopment to mini-permanent; interest typically 4% to 5% set by AMI served, term and originator; loan size up to $7.5 million; loan to value up to 150% for high-impact projects; loans must mature by August 2030.
record.affordability_requirement: Rental housing serving households at 0% to 120% AMI with deed restrictions.
record.next_deadline: Rolling through LISC Bay Area, CSH or Capital Impact; all loans must mature by August 2030.
record.layering_notes: Covers San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Alameda and Contra Costa Counties. Seeded by Chan Zuckerberg Initiative ($40 million first-loss), Facebook/Meta, Genentech, Kaiser Permanente, the San Francisco Foundation and others; underwriting tolerates more risk, including for emerging developers of color. The August 2030 maturity limit makes this a bridge product; the companion Community Housing Fund provides the long-term 2% money. The deployment goal was $500 million by end of 2025, so confirm remaining availability.
record.audit_note: Nov 8, 2026 spot check: the family of funds page does not state the five-county geography.

record.jurisdiction: Five Bay Area counties (San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Alameda, Contra Costa)
record.program_name: Partnership for the Bay's Future: Community Housing Fund (CHF) 2% long-term loans
record.administering_agency: LISC Bay Area (fund manager and originator) with Corporation for Supportive Housing and Capital Impact Partners; San Francisco Foundation convener
record.typical_award_size: $150 million fund; 2% interest; loan size up to $15 million; loan to value up to 150%; term up to 18 years with latest maturity 2038.
record.affordability_requirement: At least 20% of households housed at or below 30% AMI; Santa Clara County projects must meet the Measure A AMI definition.
record.next_deadline: Rolling through LISC Bay Area, CSH or Capital Impact.
record.layering_notes: Same five-county footprint as the Bay's Future Fund. The 2% rate and 18-year term make it usable as subordinate permanent debt alongside LIHTC and county soft loans, or as a 16-year loan in lieu of a competitive public gap source (LISC has done this). Check Measure A alignment for Santa Clara County deals.

record.jurisdiction: San Mateo County and northern Santa Clara County (15 miles from Menlo Park)
record.program_name: Catalyst Housing Fund (Meta) administered by LISC Bay Area
record.administering_agency: LISC Bay Area (administrator: underwriting, disbursement, fund and asset management) with Meta (Facebook), the City of East Palo Alto, the City of Menlo Park and Envision Transform Build; contact Lily Berticevich, Director of Community Investment
record.typical_award_size: $17 million total fund ($9 million-plus initially set aside for East Palo Alto); $75 million LISC leverage goal; 9 deals closed, $16.2 million invested, $6.5 million available; 775 units produced or preserved.
record.affordability_requirement: At least 60% of financed units affordable to low income households, of which 30% extremely low income and 30% very low income; priority for family housing and no net loss of rent-controlled or deed-restricted units.
record.layering_notes: Geography is a 15-mile radius of Meta's Menlo Park campus (roughly SFO to SJC), so it reaches San Mateo County and northern Santa Clara County cities. Projects are defined with community groups and East Palo Alto. Small remaining balance ($6.5 million), so treat as a gap or acquisition source rather than a primary lender.

record.jurisdiction: San Francisco Bay Area
record.program_name: Faith and Housing program predevelopment grants and technical assistance, LISC Bay Area
record.administering_agency: LISC Bay Area; contact Evita Chavez, Senior Program Officer, Housing; funders include Alameda County HCD, BMO, Capital One, Crankstart, First Republic Foundation, San Francisco Foundation, Silicon Valley Community Foundation, Sobrato Family Foundation and Wells Fargo
record.typical_award_size: Cohort program since 2019: technical workshops, a development coach, grant funds for predevelopment activities and a participation stipend for faith-based and community-based landowners; grant amounts not posted.
record.affordability_requirement: Affordable housing on faith-owned land, typically through a joint venture with an experienced developer.
record.next_deadline: Next cohort date not posted; join the mailing list on the program page.
record.layering_notes: Useful for developers partnering with congregations under SB 4 (Affordable Housing on Faith and Higher Education Lands Act). Grants cover early feasibility before Housing Trust or CDFI predevelopment loans. Alameda County HCD is a funder, so Alameda projects may have a direct county tie-in.

record.jurisdiction: California (Northern California focus)
record.program_name: Community Vision (formerly Northern California Community Loan Fund) affordable housing loans
record.administering_agency: Community Vision Capital and Consulting (CDFI), 870 Market Street, San Francisco; lending@communityvisionca.org
record.typical_award_size: $250,000 to $5 million (larger case by case); terms up to 10 years; loan to value up to 90%; fixed rates generally below market; 1% to 1.5% commitment fee; real estate collateral preferred, subordination to conventional lenders considered; underwriting 4 to 8 weeks after full application.
record.affordability_requirement: Affordable housing led by mission-aligned developers and other social purpose real estate serving historically underserved communities; borrowers must be California nonprofits or social enterprises.
record.layering_notes: Borrowers must be California nonprofits or social enterprises (the lending page does not limit lending to nonprofits). Community Vision is a GSAF and Bay Area TOAH originator and an FHLBank San Francisco AHP sponsor partner ($5.95 million awarded with it for 225 Bay Area units). Its Ready to Build program (separate record) provides technical assistance for first-time nonprofit developers. Good fit for community land trusts and service providers moving into housing.
record.audit_note: Nov 8, 2026 spot check: the lending page lists eligible borrowers as California nonprofits and social enterprises. Loan size, term, LTV, fees and the underwriting timeline match.

record.jurisdiction: Nine-county San Francisco Bay Area
record.program_name: Ready to Build technical assistance program for nonprofit affordable housing developers, Community Vision
record.administering_agency: Community Vision; Leslie Palaroan, Senior Program Manager, lpalaroan@communityvisionca.org
record.typical_award_size: Intensive one-on-one technical assistance (feasibility, pro forma and capital stacking, development roadmap, partner matchmaking, asset management training) for nonprofits with a project positioned to reach site acquisition, construction start or completion by December 1, 2028. No direct capital.
record.affordability_requirement: Housing affordable to households at or below 120% AMI with an identified site; preference for site control.
record.next_deadline: Applications due November 13, 2026 at 5pm (rolling if needed); selections first week of December 2026.
record.layering_notes: Open to nonprofits in the nine Bay Area counties (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano, Sonoma), including emerging developers, CLTs, faith-based entities, tribal organizations and service providers. Pairs with LISC Faith and Housing and with Community Vision or Housing Trust predevelopment loans.
record.audit_note: funding_type kept as other: Ready to Build provides fully funded technical assistance only, with no loan, grant or other deployable capital, so no money-to-project enum value fits.

record.jurisdiction: Rural California (communities of 50,000 or fewer)
record.program_name: Rural Community Assistance Corporation (RCAC) Affordable Housing Loan Program
record.administering_agency: Rural Community Assistance Corporation (CDFI), 3120 Freeboard Drive Suite 201, West Sacramento; Loan Fund 855-979-7322
record.typical_award_size: Feasibility loans normally up to $10,000, one year, 1% fee; acquisition loans up to appraised value plus fee and interest reserve, normally not more than $3 million, up to 3 years, 1% fee, may subordinate to construction lender; predevelopment loans based on line-item budget, up to 3 years, 1% fee; site development and unit construction loans normally not more than $3 million, 1.125% fee, term tied to construction period. Flyer revised May 29, 2026; funds subject to availability.
record.per_unit_cap: $3 million per loan (acquisition and construction) as a normal maximum
record.affordability_requirement: Single family and multifamily housing serving very low and low income households; RCAC finances only the low income portion of mixed income projects.
record.layering_notes: Rural only: project areas with populations of 50,000 or less. Borrowers are nonprofits, public agencies and tribal governments (no individuals). In scope for rural parts of Mendocino, Nevada, Madera, Merced, San Benito, El Dorado, Yolo, Placer, Monterey, San Luis Obispo and other counties; pairs with USDA Rural Development 514/515/538, state Joe Serna farmworker grants and county HOME or PLHA. RCAC is also a GSAF originator and a We Lift partner in the Coachella Valley.
record.audit_note: Nov 8, 2026 spot check: the flyer revised May 29, 2026 also notes short-term rates generally in the 5 percent range and that the normal maximums are policy limits, so higher amounts can be approved.

record.jurisdiction: California (Orange County headquarters, statewide)
record.program_name: Clearinghouse CDFI commercial real estate secured loans for multifamily affordable housing
record.administering_agency: Clearinghouse Community Development Financial Institution, 23861 El Toro Road Suite 401, Lake Forest (Orange County); pre-application at clearinghousecdfi.com/borrowers
record.typical_award_size: Minimum loan $1,000,000; acquisition, refinance, construction, renovation and gap financing secured by real estate; case-by-case structures; also New Markets Tax Credit allocations ($10 million NMTC plus $4.1 million source loan to Heritage Housing Partners for Napa Redwood Housing, 40 affordable condos, 2026). Clearinghouse secured $100 million through the Treasury CDFI Bond Guarantee Program.
record.affordability_requirement: Multifamily affordable and special needs housing serving low income households; mixed-use and mobile home parks also eligible.
record.layering_notes: Orange County based, statewide and multi-state lender with FHLBank San Francisco membership (sponsors AHP grants, including tribal housing awards). Northern California deals opened this pass: Napa Redwood Housing (2026) and a Brilliant Corners enhanced behavioral support home in Vacaville (2022, $741,000). Also a frequent lender in San Diego, Orange and Riverside Counties. Works for for-profit and nonprofit borrowers and public or tribal entities.
record.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: clearinghousecdfi.com returned 403 to curl and WebFetch on the borrowers page and home page; no official substitute host found. Facts not re-checked.

record.jurisdiction: Northern California and Bay Area region (statewide lender)
record.program_name: Corporation for Supportive Housing (CSH) project initiation, predevelopment, acquisition and mini-perm loans
record.administering_agency: Corporation for Supportive Housing (national CDFI) with California lending staff; loans@csh.org
record.typical_award_size: Term sheet dated June 1, 2025: project initiation loans $50,000 to $100,000 at 0% to 3% for 24 months, 3-year term, unsecured, no fee; predevelopment $150,000 to $2 million at 7.5% fixed, 3 years, LTV up to 130% (no LTV test under $500,000), 1.5% origination; acquisition $150,000 to $15 million at 7.5% fixed, 3 years, 100% LTV on property plus 130% for predevelopment, 1.5% origination; mini-perm $150,000 to $1 million at 7.5% fixed, 5 years, 100% LTV. Construction gap loans where a lead lender monitors draws (Capital Magnet Fund blended rates). Rates published monthly and locked at full application.
record.affordability_requirement: Affordable housing that includes supportive housing; borrowers are nonprofit, for-profit or public agencies with a supportive or affordable housing track record.
record.layering_notes: CSH will lend well over 100% of collateral value, which fits early-stage supportive housing before Homekey+, NPLH, BHSA or county Measure A commitments. CSH is a GSAF originator, a Bay Area TOAH originator and an originator for the Partnership for the Bay's Future funds. Rates (7.5%) are higher than Housing Trust or Destination: Home money, so use CSH where those are unavailable or for non-Bay Area counties.

record.jurisdiction: California (San Francisco Bay Area core geography)
record.program_name: Capital Impact Partners (Momentus Capital) acquisition and predevelopment loans
record.administering_agency: Capital Impact Partners, part of Momentus Capital (CDFI, Oakland office); California contact Eric Relos, erelos@capitalimpact.org, 510-712-9021
record.typical_award_size: December 2025 term sheet: $500,000 to $15 million for non-operating properties and $500,000 to $20 million for operating properties; term up to 3 years plus two 1-year extensions (operating properties up to 10 years); fixed rate at Treasury plus 4% to 5% or floating 30-day SOFR plus 3.5% to 4.5%, lower with special funding sources; interest only; no prepayment fee for terms of 3 years or less; origination 1% to 1.5% (includes 0.25% underwriting fee), legal typically $30,000 to $35,000; 5% to 10% equity including subordinate debt and grants; 60 to 90 day closings. Also construction, rehabilitation, mini-permanent (up to 90% LTV), bridge and NMTC products.
record.affordability_requirement: No AMI test stated in Capital Impact term sheets; loans fund mission-aligned acquisition and predevelopment for housing, healthcare, education, commercial and mixed-use projects, with preference for core geographies (California is one).
record.layering_notes: The San Francisco Bay Area is one of Momentus Capital's core geographies and Capital Impact originates for the Partnership for the Bay's Future Bay's Future Fund and Community Housing Fund (lower rates than its standard sheet). Full recourse to sponsors; first lien preferred, second lien case by case. Its CDFI Equitable Recovery award funds a housing developer training and capital access program that expanded into the Bay Area.
record.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: the prior 80% AMI or low-moderate income tract requirement was not found on the source page, the December 2025 acquisition and predevelopment term sheet, or the construction, mini-perm, lending process and offerings sheets. Dollar terms match the December 2025 sheet.

record.jurisdiction: FHLBank San Francisco district (California, Arizona, Nevada)
record.program_name: FHLBank San Francisco Affordable Housing Program (AHP) General Fund competitive grants
record.administering_agency: Federal Home Loan Bank of San Francisco (member-sponsored applications; the project sponsor applies through an FHLBank member bank, credit union, insurer or CDFI)
record.typical_award_size: 2026 competition: $60.1 million in General Fund grants awarded June 22, 2026 to 39 projects (2,676 units) in California and Arizona from 125 applications; 2026 awards total $66.3 million including the Nevada Targeted Fund, up nearly one-third from 2025. Per the 2026 Implementation Plan, maximum request is the lesser of $2,000,000 or 50% of total project costs, and no more than $65,000 per income-restricted rental unit (scored on a declining scale from $30,000 to $65,000). Four years from award to complete construction and draw funds. Since 1990, $1.48 billion awarded for nearly 160,000 homes.
record.per_unit_cap: $65,000 per income-restricted rental unit and $2,000,000 per project (lesser of $2,000,000 or 50% of total project costs)
record.affordability_requirement: Rental projects must reserve at least 20% of units for households at or below 50% AMI with a 15-year retention period; owner-occupied projects serve households at or below 80% AMI (5-year retention).
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. 2026 General Fund awards announced June 22, 2026; FHLBank San Francisco has not posted 2027 competition dates.
record.layering_notes: A grant that flows through a member institution, so line up a member bank or CDFI sponsor (Housing Trust Silicon Valley, Community Vision and Clearinghouse CDFI are members that sponsor awards) early. Scoring favors homelessness and special needs set-asides, ELI units, lower subsidy per unit and donated or discounted property; 2026 awards included $27.9 million for 19 supportive housing developments and more than $20 million for 12 senior developments. Loan pools and revolving funds may not apply to the General Fund. AHP funds are private bank-system money and do not by themselves trigger state prevailing wage, though federal AHP regulations apply. Grants are typically sized at $30,000 to $65,000 per unit and used as gap equity alongside LIHTC and state soft debt.
record.cycle_notes: Annual General Fund competition under the yearly AHP Implementation Plan (2026 plan effective January 1, 2026). 2026 awards announced June 22, 2026. The AHP and Apply pages invite unfunded applicants to reapply in the 2027 competition but give no application window; the 2026 Implementation Plan sets no round dates. Check for the 2027 Implementation Plan and window, which on past cycles would fall in the first half of the year (not stated by the Bank).
record.audit_note: Tier 2 deadline audit 2026-11-08: no 2027 round dates posted. 2026 Implementation Plan confirms $2,000,000 or 50% of total project cost cap, $65,000 per rental unit cap and 20% at 50% AMI.

record.jurisdiction: CommonSpirit Health hospital markets in California
record.program_name: CommonSpirit Health (Dignity Health) Community Investment Program below-market loans
record.administering_agency: CommonSpirit Health Community Investment Program, San Francisco; cip@commonspirit.org; expression of interest form on the program page; local Dignity Health hospitals act as community liaisons
record.typical_award_size: Loans up to $10.0 million, tenor up to 10 years, secured or unsecured, concessionary interest benchmarked to inflation, flexible repayment; structures include bridge, line of credit and term. $400 million allocation; $263 million approved across 94 investments as of March 31, 2025; 398 loans and $502.5 million approved since 1990, with affordable housing about 45% of the portfolio. Dignity Health's Homeless Health Initiative has invested nearly $36 million across its California sites since FY2019, including $375,000 in May 2026 for two Yolo County projects ($125,000 Freeman Garden Court, Woodland, 12 units; $250,000 Choice Neighborhoods and Tupelo project, 73 units) and more than $3 million in Yolo and Sacramento Counties to date.
record.affordability_requirement: Mission-oriented projects addressing social drivers of health, including affordable and supportive housing for low income communities; must show community support and partnership with a CommonSpirit hospital.
record.layering_notes: Place-based: investments are tied to CommonSpirit (Dignity Health) hospital markets, which in scope include Sacramento (Mercy General, Mercy San Juan, Methodist, Mercy Folsom, Woodland Memorial in Yolo), Stockton (St. Joseph's, San Joaquin), Merced, Grass Valley (Sierra Nevada Memorial, Nevada County), Redwood City (Sequoia, San Mateo), Santa Cruz (Dominican), San Luis Obispo and Santa Maria, Ventura (St. John's) and the Inland Empire. Loans often go through a CDFI or linked deposit; CommonSpirit also guarantees loans. Dignity Health is a financing partner of the Monterey Bay Housing Trust. Patient, concessionary money that fits predevelopment or gap positions in supportive housing with co-located services.
eligible_project_detail: bridge and lines of credit to developers and CDFIs
record.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: program PDF matches loan size up to $10.0M, 10-year tenor, concessionary rate, $400M allocation, $263M and 398 loans/$502.5M as of March 31, 2025 (the web page text shows an older 386 loans/$454M). Page lists inquiry email cip-inquiry@commonspirit.org. Homeless Health Initiative figures were not re-checked on this source.

record.jurisdiction: Santa Clara, San Mateo, San Francisco, Alameda and Santa Cruz Counties
record.program_name: Bay Area Housing Innovation Fund (Housing Accelerator Fund with Apple, Sobrato Philanthropies and Destination: Home)
record.administering_agency: Housing Accelerator Fund (San Francisco nonprofit lender), with founding partners Apple, Sobrato Philanthropies and Destination: Home; later investors Valhalla Foundation, Harry and Jeanette Weinberg Foundation and individual philanthropists
record.typical_award_size: $100 million fund (launched July 2024 at $50 million, doubled December 2025). Mezzanine construction-to-permanent loans (September 2025 term sheet): up to $20 million per project, higher on request; construction period interest about 3% to 5% fixed; permanent period subordinate debt repaid from residual receipts and refinance proceeds to a 5% target annualized return; total term up to 20 years; origination up to 1%. Construction-to-permanent first mortgage loans (August 2025 term sheet) with the same $20 million cap, 3% to 5% construction pricing and 20-year maximum. Loans to date: $16 million for 1633 Valencia, San Francisco (Mercy Housing California, 145 PSH units, 19-month build, about $525,000 per unit) and $11 million for Harvey West Studios, Santa Cruz (Housing Matters with MidPen, 120 PSH units).
record.per_unit_cap: Total development cost caps excluding land: under $575,000 per unit for studio projects, $650,000 for small-unit projects, $700,000 for all one-bedroom projects and $775,000 for family projects
record.affordability_requirement: Net new permanently affordable units up to 120% AMI with preference for 50% and 30% AMI; nearly half of pilot homes reserved for formerly homeless or extremely low income households.
record.next_deadline: Rolling after entitlement; a NOFA is forthcoming (sign up on the fund page). Construction must start within 12 months of commitment and reach certificate of occupancy within 3 years.
record.layering_notes: Eligible counties: Santa Clara, San Mateo, San Francisco, Alameda and Santa Cruz. Intended to let projects skip the LIHTC queue: it funds construction and permanent debt for projects that commit to cost and time targets about 40% below Bay Area averages, with a third-party evaluator documenting the approach. Entitlements must be in hand before commitment. Pairs with county Measure A or local gap funds, Homekey+ and project-based vouchers; residual receipts split must follow local public agency policy where applicable.
record.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check November 8, 2026: term sheets match $20M cap, 3% to 5% construction pricing, 5% mezz target return, 20-year term, TDC caps, 120% AMI with 50% and 30% preference, five counties, entitlement and 12-month start rules. Perm loan sheet also states about 6% permanent period rate. Fund page now lists 1633 Valencia at $540,000 per home (record says about $525,000) and Harvey West at $530,000 per home.
